Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corporation Bankruptcy Case

Applicant: Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corporation. Domicile: No. 319, Huanshi East Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Mai Zhinan, General Manager of the Corporation.

On January 11, 1999, Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as GITIC) filed an application for bankruptcy with the Guangdong High People's Court on the grounds of severe insolvency and inability to pay its huge maturing debts.

The Guangdong High People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

GITIC was originally named Guangdong Trust and Investment Corporation, registered and established with the Guangzhou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce in July 1980 upon approval by the People's Government of Guangdong Province as a wholly state-owned enterprise legal person. In 1983, it was approved by the People's Bank of China as a non-bank financial institution with the right to engage in foreign exchange operations; in March 1984, it was registered with the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce and changed its name to Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corporation, with registered capital of RMB 1.2 billion. Since 1992, due to chaotic management, GITIC engaged in a large number of irregular business activities such as absorbing deposits at high interest rates, off-balance-sheet operations, arbitrary interbank borrowing, and arbitrary investments, resulting in its inability to pay huge domestic and foreign debts upon maturity and severe insolvency. On October 6, 1998, the People's Bank of China decided to close GITIC and organized a closure liquidation team to conduct closure liquidation. During the closure liquidation period, GITIC's financial business and related claims and debts were entrusted to Bank of China for management, and GITIC's securities trading business departments were entrusted to GF Securities Co., Ltd. for management, with their business operations continuing as usual. The three-month closure liquidation from October 6, 1998 to January 6, 1999 found that GITIC's total assets were RMB 21.471 billion, total liabilities were RMB 36.165 billion, the overall asset-liability ratio was 168.23%, and the deficit was RMB 14.694 billion. On January 11, 1999, Bank of China issued the "Announcement on the Settlement of Claims of Natural Persons against the Former Provincial International Trust and Investment Corporation", stating that in view of GITIC's severe insolvency and inability to repay huge debts, the settlement of claims of natural persons would only pay the principal, not the interest; after Bank of China settled the claims of natural persons against GITIC, the Guangdong Branch of Bank of China would, on behalf of the Guangdong Provincial Department of Finance, declare claims in accordance with the law and receive distribution as an ordinary creditor in the order of bankruptcy distribution.

The Guangdong High People's Court held: Article 3, Item 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) (hereinafter referred to as the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law) provides: "If an enterprise suffers serious losses due to poor management and is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, it shall be declared bankrupt in accordance with the provisions of this Law." Article 8 provides: "A debtor may, with the consent of its competent superior department, apply to be declared bankrupt." GITIC was extremely chaotic in management, severely insolvent, and unable to pay its huge domestic and foreign debts as they fell due, meeting the conditions for bankruptcy as provided by law. On January 16, 1999, it ruled:

1. GITIC shall undergo bankruptcy liquidation.
2. A liquidation team shall be appointed to take over GITIC.

After the ruling was announced, the bankruptcy liquidation work of GITIC proceeded according to law in the following steps:

1. Declaration, Examination, and Confirmation of Claims

On January 16, 1999, the Guangdong High People's Court published announcements in the People's Daily and the People's Court Daily regarding the acceptance of the bankruptcy application of GITIC, requiring creditors to declare their claims within three months from the date of the announcement; failure to declare within the time limit would be deemed as automatic waiver. Other civil enforcement proceedings against GITIC were suspended according to law, and applicants for enforcement could declare their claims based on effective legal instruments; other civil proceedings against GITIC were also terminated or suspended according to law. Within the announcement period, a total of 320 creditors declared claims, with the total declared claim amount being RMB 38.77738 billion (including 167 foreign creditors declaring claims of RMB 32.01297 billion).

On April 22, 1999, the Guangdong High People's Court presided over the first creditors' meeting in the GITIC bankruptcy case, with representatives from 244 domestic and foreign creditors attending, accounting for 76% of the total number of declaring creditors. The court informed the creditors of the functions and powers of the creditors' meeting, and based on the amounts of claims declared by each creditor, appointed nine creditors, including Swiss Bank, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank of Japan, Citibank of the United States, and Bank of China, to form the Creditors' Chairman Committee. The bankruptcy liquidation team reported to the representatives attending the creditors' meeting on the situation of claim declaration. The meeting approved the principles for the disposal of GITIC's bankruptcy property proposed by the bankruptcy liquidation team.

After recording and examining the claims declared by creditors, the bankruptcy liquidation team notified each claim declarant of the examination results, either by confirming the claim or rejecting the declaration. For claims confirmed by the liquidation team without objection from the creditor, the liquidation team submitted them to the creditors' meeting for voting and approval; if a claim declarant objected to the confirmation result of the liquidation team, they submitted it to the Guangdong High People's Court for a ruling.

Based on the applications of claim objectors, the Guangdong High People's Court respectively conducted public hearings on 62 objections concerning claim declarations in the GITIC bankruptcy case and issued rulings accordingly:

(1) All secured claims based on comfort letters were denied. In the litigation for claim confirmation, 15 creditors of GITIC's Hong Kong subsidiaries held comfort letters issued by GITIC to declare secured (or contingent) claims amounting to approximately RMB 2.3 billion, requesting confirmation. The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that, in terms of form, the comfort letters were not contracts signed between GITIC and specific creditors but were introductory letters issued to unspecified third parties; in terms of content, the comfort letters did not express any intention to provide a guarantee and did not stipulate that, upon the debtor's failure to perform its obligations, the issuer would perform or assume liability for repayment. Therefore, the comfort letters did not constitute a guarantee under Chinese law and had no legal effect of guarantee suretyship. All secured claims based on comfort letters were rejected.

(2) Depositors of trust deposits could declare bankruptcy claims but had no right of reclamation over such deposits. In the litigation for claim confirmation, 17 creditors declared claims totaling RMB 3.8 billion to the bankruptcy liquidation team of GITIC based on trust deposits. Some domestic creditors argued that trust deposits were trust property with independence, that the trustee GITIC did not have ownership of the trust property but only the right to manage and operate it, and that ownership of the trust property belonged to the trustor, requesting to exercise the right of reclamation. The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that GITIC issued trust deposit certificates to depositors, stipulating that the depositors would deposit funds with GITIC and retrieve the principal and interest upon maturity, which had the characteristics of a deposit contract. The relationship between the depositors and GITIC was a creditor-debtor relationship, not a trust relationship. After GITIC was declared bankrupt, the remaining deposits should be confirmed as bankruptcy claims, and the depositors did not have the right of reclamation.

(3) Confirmation of bankruptcy claims declared by creditors based on swap contracts. Creditors who declared bankruptcy claims based on swap transactions with GITIC objected to the bankruptcy liquidation team's rejection and filed objections with the court. The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that interest rate swap transactions are a financial method widely adopted internationally, aimed at reducing financing costs and guarding against risks from interest rate fluctuations. The key to confirming bankruptcy claims based on swap contracts was to determine whether such interest rate swap transactions required case-by-case approval from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and to assess whether the interest rate swap transaction was for hedging or speculation. GITIC held a "License for Operating Foreign Exchange Business" issued by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and its scope of foreign exchange business included proprietary and customer foreign exchange trading. Therefore, GITIC had the legal capacity to engage in hedging derivative financial instrument transactions and did not require case-by-case approval from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. If the interest rate swap transaction between the parties involved a corresponding underlying instrument transaction, rather than purely based on predictions of price trends of derivative financial instruments in the market, then it was a hedging derivative financial instrument transaction, and such interest rate swap transaction was confirmed as valid. After the creditors provided market quotations agreed by both parties to calculate losses and verified that the termination of the swap agreement due to GITIC's closure had caused losses, the bankruptcy claims declared by the creditors were confirmed.

(4) Commercial banks and their branches could set off the total amount of claims they held against GITIC against the total amount of debts they owed to GITIC on an equal basis before bankruptcy liquidation. According to Article 33 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, which provides that "A creditor who owes debts to the bankrupt enterprise may set off those debts before bankruptcy liquidation", and Article 22 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "Branches of a commercial bank do not have the status of a legal person and conduct business within the scope authorized by the head office, with the civil liability borne by the head office", commercial banks and their branches could set off the total amount of claims they held against GITIC against the total amount of debts they owed to GITIC on an equal basis before bankruptcy liquidation. After each commercial bank branch declared its claim separately, the commercial bank would uniformly exercise the right of set-off. The bankruptcy liquidation team of GITIC handled the set-off of claims and debts with commercial banks such as Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and China Construction Bank in accordance with the law.

The Guangdong High People's Court ultimately confirmed that there were a total of 200 creditors in the GITIC bankruptcy case, with a total claim amount of RMB 20.22317 billion.

2. Examination, Confirmation, and Disposal of Bankruptcy Property

The bankruptcy liquidation team of GITIC determined upon liquidation that the total assets on GITIC's books at the time of the bankruptcy declaration were RMB 20.93748 billion. Parties who objected to the bankruptcy liquidation team's determination of bankruptcy property submitted their objections to the Guangdong High People's Court for a ruling in accordance with the law.

Based on the applications of the parties, the Guangdong High People's Court confirmed the following objections by ruling:

(1) It was confirmed that the 100% equity in Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. originally registered under the names of Guangdong Trust and Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Real Estate Company) and Guangxin Industrial Co., Ltd. (in liquidation) (hereinafter referred to as Guangxin Company) constituted bankruptcy property of GITIC. Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. was a cooperative joint venture (with Hong Kong capital) nominally owned by Real Estate Company and Guangxin Company. The bankruptcy liquidation team considered that GITIC was actually its investing company and that its equity should belong to GITIC, requesting Real Estate Company and Guangxin Company to deliver the 50% equity held by each respectively. The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that although the Chinese investor of Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. was registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce as Real Estate Company and the foreign investor as Guangxin Company, with GITIC only being its supervising department, Real Estate Company did not perform its capital contribution obligations, and Guangxin Company's capital contribution actually originated from GITIC. To enable the Building Industry Company to enjoy the preferential policies for Sino-foreign cooperative enterprises, GITIC decided to establish Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. to be responsible for the operation and management of Guangdong International Building, and arranged for its wholly-owned subsidiary Real Estate Company and Hong Kong-registered Guangxin Company to act as the Chinese and foreign shareholders of the Building Industry Company. Since both Real Estate Company and Guangxin Company failed to perform the most basic shareholder obligation of capital contribution, neither was a lawful shareholder. As the actual capital contributor to Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd., GITIC was entitled to ownership of the company. Accordingly, it was ruled that the 100% equity in Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. belonged to GITIC.

(2) It was confirmed that GITIC's investment rights and interests in its wholly-owned subsidiaries constituted bankruptcy property. GITIC had 29 wholly-owned subsidiaries. The bankruptcy liquidation team, based on different circumstances, defined the scope of recovery of GITIC's investment rights and interests. For wholly-owned subsidiaries with good business conditions and profitability, the method of overall transfer was adopted to recover the investment rights and interests; for subsidiaries with insolvency and negative investment equity values, closure and liquidation or application for bankruptcy were decided according to law. For equity and income formed by GITIC's external investments, recovery was primarily through the sale or transfer of equity, but recovery was stopped where the equity value was negative.

(3) It was confirmed that the ownership of the margin deposits of stock investors collected by GITIC's securities trading business departments belonged to the investors. GITIC's four securities trading business departments were its branches. Because these securities trading business departments had long mixed investor margin deposits with their own funds, engaged in irregular operations, and misappropriated large amounts of investor margin deposits, a shortfall in investor margin funds occurred, amounting to RMB 70.52 million as of January 16, 1999. The bankruptcy liquidation team considered that after the misappropriation of investor margin deposits, investors could only declare claims to the liquidation team and had no right of reclamation. The Guangdong High People's Court held upon trial that margin deposits were settlement funds entrusted by investors to GITIC's securities business departments for the purpose of purchasing and selling stocks on their behalf; the securities business departments were only custodians, and the act of investors depositing margin deposits with securities institutions constituted a mandate, which did not alter the nature of ownership and the right to use the margin deposits. The failure of the securities business department to establish a separate margin account for segregated management was the fault of the securities trading business department and did not mean that the ownership of the margin deposits had changed. The securities trading business departments were branches of GITIC. After GITIC's bankruptcy, the stock owners could, according to law, retrieve the margin deposits through the bankruptcy liquidation team. Accordingly, it was ruled that investors could retrieve the balance of margin deposits for stock trading.

For property confirmed by law as belonging to GITIC, the Guangdong High People's Court proceeded with recovery or realization in different circumstances:

For GITIC's claims within Guangdong Province, the Guangdong High People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on the Unified Management of Enforcement Work by High People's Courts", ruled to designate enforcement by 58 courts at the location of GITIC's debtors, recovering a total of RMB 1.51 billion.

For GITIC's property in other provinces, municipalities, and autonomous regions, the bankruptcy liquidation team recovered it according to law, totaling RMB 538.23 million.

For GITIC's property in foreign countries and regions such as the United States and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the bankruptcy liquidation team recovered it in accordance with local laws, totaling an equivalent of RMB 229.84 million in investments and loans.

Regarding the issue that 69 government agencies within Guangdong Province provided guarantees for GITIC's debtors, which were confirmed as invalid and should bear corresponding compensation liability, the Guangdong High People's Court entrusted the Guangdong Audit Department to organize audit teams to audit the extrabudgetary funds of these government agencies one by one. Based on the audit results, compulsory enforcement was carried out against the extrabudgetary funds of these government agencies according to law. For government agencies without extrabudgetary funds, the court handled the suspension of enforcement procedures according to law, recovering a total of RMB 76.25 million.

All bankruptcy property of GITIC was realized through auction or competitive bidding. Among them: the 100% equity of GITIC in Guangdong Commodity Exhibition and Sales Center was successfully auctioned at RMB 389 million; through competitive bidding, GITIC's four securities trading business departments were transferred to GF Securities Co., Ltd. at RMB 80.93 million; the 75% equity and claims of GITIC in Jiangwan New City was successfully auctioned at RMB 350 million; the 100% equity and claims of GITIC in Guangdong International Building Industry Co., Ltd. was successfully auctioned at RMB 1.13 billion.

3. Distribution of Bankruptcy Property and Conclusion of Bankruptcy Proceedings

After the recovery and realization of GITIC's bankruptcy property, the costs of bankruptcy liquidation (including professional service fees of intermediaries, evaluation fees, and other liquidation expenses) were paid in priority according to law. Creditors' meetings were held on October 31, 2000, June 28, 2002, and February 28, 2003, respectively. After the priority payment of wages owed to employees, labor insurance premiums, and taxes owed, bankruptcy claims were distributed in proportion in three installments. With the approval of the Guangdong High People's Court by ruling, the bankruptcy property was distributed in three installments, with a total distribution of RMB 2.534 billion, and an overall claim satisfaction rate of 12.52%. For claims of foreign creditors, with the consent of the foreign exchange administration department, they were all converted into foreign currency for payment.

After the completion of the relevant judicial procedures in the GITIC bankruptcy case, the bankruptcy liquidation team applied to conclude the bankruptcy proceedings according to law. The Guangdong High People's Court, upon review, held that in the case of GITIC's application for bankruptcy, the claim confirmation work had been completed, the scope of bankruptcy property had been defined, all effective legal measures had been taken for the recovery of external claims, the main bankruptcy property of GITIC had been auctioned and realized and distributed to creditors, and the GITIC bankruptcy case had met the statutory conditions for concluding bankruptcy proceedings. However, since there were still recoverable bankruptcy property and follow-up matters such as supplementary distribution to be handled, the bankruptcy liquidation team should be retained to continue being responsible for completing the recovery of bankruptcy property and supplementary distribution. Therefore, while granting the bankruptcy liquidation team's application to conclude the bankruptcy proceedings, the bankruptcy liquidation team should continue to be retained to handle the relevant follow-up matters. Accordingly, on March 8, 2003, in accordance with Article 38 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and Article 97 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases", it ruled:

(1) The bankruptcy proceedings of the GITIC bankruptcy case are concluded.
(2) GITIC's bankruptcy liquidation team shall, based on this ruling, go through the cancellation of registration of GITIC with the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce.
(3) GITIC's bankruptcy liquidation team is retained to complete follow-up matters such as the recovery of GITIC's bankruptcy property and supplementary distribution.

Court costs in this case are reduced by half and shall be paid from the bankruptcy estate with priority.
